title: Predicting Airline Satisfaction
source: kaggle REST API, Basic auth from ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json

endpoints.leaderboard_limit: returns only the top 20 rows; /api/i/competitions.LeaderboardService/GetLeaderboard returns 403 with these credentials, so the full 754-team table is not retrievable this way

our_state.gap_in_paired_noise_floors: 0.00078 / 0.0002 = ~3.9x the measured paired public-LB noise floor of +-0.0002, so the gap is real signal, not noise

observations: The top 20 occupy a 1.0e-4 band (0.961660 to 0.961760) and every one of them scores at or above 0.9616. That is a converged pack, not a long tail: the leader is only 1e-4 ahead of rank 20.
The gap from US to the leader is 7.8e-4, which is roughly 2.6x the 3e-4 rank-1-to-rank-45 spread noted earlier. So there is MORE headroom now than the earlier reading suggested.

Our OOF 0.961509 sits 5.3e-4 ABOVE our public 0.960980. That difference is smaller than the public split's standalone AUC SE (~0.0015, since the public split is 59,969 rows), so it is consistent with noise and must NOT be read as a systematic OOF optimism correction.
Leaderboard top rose from ~0.9616 to 0.96176 since the last refresh, consistent with the 59-member-scale approaches still improving.
